transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~10 minutes
Attendees: Lena Martin (Redwood AE), Diego Suarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Equinox Head of Partnerships), Marco Li (Equinox Cloud Partnerships), Sofia Redding (Equinox Solutions Architect)

Auto-summary: quick intro, partnership interest for Equinox to resell / integrate Redwood inference for their customers; technical notes on private deployment options and benchmarks; security checklist items requested.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, I'm the partner AE, with Diego from our solutions team. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Priya: Hi Lena, thanks, doing well. Excited to learn more. Marco and Sofia are here as well.
[00:18] Marco: Yep hi all.
[00:20] Diego: Great, we'll keep this high level for the first 10 then go deeper on infra if you want. Quick agenda: intro, what Equinox is looking to do, where Redwood fits, security/compliance Qs, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:32] Priya: Sounds great.
[00:35] Lena: Cool. Briefly about Redwood — we're a developer-first inference platform that supports hosted API, dedicated reserved pools and private deployments. We focus on predictable latency, cost controls, and tooling for rollouts and observability. Apologies if I mangle anything, our product names are Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console — sometimes the robo-transcript calls it 'Redwood dedicates' — so forgive me.
[01:05] Sofia: Quick q — Equinox runs a managed GPU marketplace, we want to offer inference endpoints to our customers but with options: 1) direct resell where we host, 2) integration where customer self-hosts on Equinox infra, or 3) white-label managed offering. We're trying to understand which Redwood deployment fits each.
[01:26] Diego: Totally. Hosted API is easiest for go-to-market, minimal ops; Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infra for higher throughput and isolation; Private is basically a VPC/on-prem package when customers need network isolation or specific KMS/HSM controls. For a marketplace you could offer multiple models — e.g., default hosted for SMBs, and private for enterprise customers.
[01:50] Marco: For the private option, how does networking work? We need to know inbound/outbound, VPC peering, whether we can run the control plane in our network.
[01:59] Diego: For our Private deployment we do a customer-managed control plane pattern. You can either run the control plane in your VPC or we ship a package for on-prem. We do SAML/SSO integration for IAM, and we support KMS integrations — you can bring your own KMS or use a supported cloud KMS. We also have audit logs and retention controls.
[02:24] Marco: OK, and encryption at rest — HSM?
[02:27] Lena: We integrate with HSM/KMS depending on the deployment. For fully air-gapped on-prem, we support offline key management patterns but that'll be part of an enterprise agreement.
[02:36] Priya: Awesome. Another concern — latency. Our customers buy GPUs for low-latency inference, they will ask about LLM hop latency and kv cache behavior. Any benchmarks?
[02:47] Diego: We have public benchmarks but we'll run partner-specific tests. Typical LLM + token latencies vary by model and quantization; we optimize kernels dynamically and do continuous batching with the K/V cache. Quick caveat, transcripts often flip KV cache to 'k v cache' or 'kay v' so ignore the weirdness.
[03:06] Sofia: (laughs) noted. For the benchmarks, what telemetry do you surface? We need tracing per route and token-level cost breakdown for billing.
[03:15] Diego: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, traces, and rollout history. You can export metrics to Prometheus, or push to your observability platform.
[03:27] Marco: What about model variants and fallback? If we run out of capacity in a region — can you route to cheaper variants?
[03:34] Lena: Yes, smart routing lets you route by latency/cost/region and fallback to compatible variants. That's useful for graceful degradation.
[03:42] Priya: Commercially, are you open to marketplace-style rev share, or is it strictly reseller with committed capacity?
[03:50] Lena: We're flexible — standard is usage-based for hosted, reserved monthly commits for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing for Private. For a marketplace, we've done rev-share pilot deals; we'd need to scope expected volume and SLAs.
[04:03] Priya: Great. Marco, Sofia — anything on your side re: integration priorities?
[04:08] Marco: We need an indicator for multi-tenant billing; per-customer metering is critical. Also want to know about per-tenant model pinning and rollout control so customers can test model upgrades.
[04:20] Diego: We have per-route and token attribution which can be used for per-tenant billing, and model pinning with canary rollouts. Ops team can configure canaries and automatic fallback policies.
[04:31] Sofia: Security checklist — SOC 2? ISO? Pen testing? We will need copies for our compliance team.
[04:38] Lena: We can share SOC 2 Type II, ISO certs if available, pen-test summaries, network diagrams and our security pack. I'll attach a security binder.
[04:48] Priya: Nice. Any red flags we should be aware of?
[04:51] Diego: Not really, just that certain enterprise features — e.g., HSM passthrough in air-gapped mode — require legal and a professional services engagement to validate. Also for on-prem we need to size GPU pools carefully; sometimes marketplace customers assume a small number of GPUs can handle high concurrency — that needs benchmarking.
[05:09] Priya: OK understood.
[05:12] Marco: A technical question on quantization — do you have mixed precision or INT8 variants supported out of the box? Our customers often ask for cost-efficient models.
[05:21] Diego: We support several quantization profiles, and the runtime selects kernels for the model architecture and sequence length. We can provide recommendations during the benchmark run. Sometimes the transcript system writes 'intate' when we say 'INT8' so apologies for that.
[05:34] Sofia: Ha, these transcripts are getting personality.
[05:36] Lena: Logistics: if we were to run a pilot, we'd want 4–6 week POC with specific success criteria — e.g., 95th pct latency under X ms for N tokens, cost per 1k tokens under Y for the chosen model, and integration checklist items like SSO and billing hooks.
[05:56] Priya: That timeline sounds reasonable. We'll have to validate with our GTM and legal teams.
[06:02] Marco: On the legal/commercial side, we have typical reseller terms, and for marketplace listing we'll need an SLA for availability and responsible disclosure around vulnerabilities.
[06:12] Lena: We can surface our SLA tiers — hosted has our standard uptime, dedicated can be SLA-backed with capacity commitments. We'll include the SLA language in the packet.
[06:23] Priya: Question from my side — how does Redwood handle model weights licensing? Some vendors require licensing for commercial hosting.
[06:31] Diego: We onboard both open and commercially-licensed models; we track model licensing and can help with vetting. For marketplace customers, that will be a joint responsibility to confirm licensing terms.
[06:44] Marco: For billing and metering integration, do you have APIs?
[06:47] Lena: Yes we expose usage APIs and webhooks, and you can pull per-route token usage. We can provide a sample billing integration.
[06:55] Sofia: Great. Regarding deployment, will we be able to offer a fully self-hosted image in Equinox catalog for customers who want to spin up a private instance?
[07:04] Diego: Yes, for white-label self-hosted patterns we can provide an image and a deployment manifest. For air-gapped installs there are extra steps but it's supported.
[07:15] Priya: Anything about multi-region? We have customers in EU that require EU-only data residency.
[07:21] Lena: We support region pinning — you can route requests to EU regions only and pin model variants. For Private deployments you can run in your EU region or on-prem. We'll note residency in the security packet.
[07:33] Marco: Ok show of hands — are there specific data retention or logs duration questions?
[07:38] Sofia: Our compliance folks typically want 365 days of audit logs, ability to redact PII on request.
[07:44] Diego: Audit log retention is configurable; PII redaction workflows can be integrated at the app layer or via post-processing. We'll include options.
[07:53] Priya: Great. Any competitors you're worried about in this context?
[07:57] Lena: We see vendor competition from cloud providers and inference runtimes — NVIDIA's offerings, Lambda, AuroraCloud for managed infra; but we differentiate on unified tooling and observability.
[08:08] Marco: Ok. Can we talk technical deep-dive next? Maybe a separate call with our infra leads — GPU provisioning, kernel tuning, and benchmark plan.
[08:16] Diego: Absolutely. We recommend a 60–90 minute tech deep-dive with our infra SEs that covers model selection, quantization choices, traffic shaping, and a runbook for the benchmark.
[08:26] Priya: Let's do that. We'll propose times next week.
[08:29] Lena: Quick recap of next steps: I'll send the partner deck + pricing grid + security pack; Diego will draft a benchmark plan and sample metrics template; Priya will introduce infra leads. We'll also propose dates for the tech deep-dive.
[08:45] Marco: Sounds good.
[08:47] Sofia: One last question — what's the level of PS needed to spin a private deployment on Equinox for a pilot?
[08:53] Diego: Typically a small PS engagement for setup, networking, and HSM integration — estimate 2–4 engineer-weeks depending on complexity. We'll put a ballpark in the follow-up.
[09:06] Lena: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
[09:10] Priya: Thanks Lena, Diego.
[09:12] Marco: Thank you.
[09:13] Sofia: Thanks.

Call end.

References / shared artifacts: partner-deck-v2.pdf (link in chat), Redwood security pack (link), benchmark-template.xlsx (link).

Notes on transcript quality: some names and acronyms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' or 'K V cache', 'INT8' sometimes misheard). The transcript purposely retains spoken style and occasional stutters.
